ops.title: ParavirtualizedGraphicsGPUTask semantics + measured 2026-07-14 results: display sleep = 0% CPU (total win, codified for metal), resolution shrink = no effect, fresh-boot 15-25% vs multi-day ~2%, live-task identification recipe
ops.body:
`com.apple.gpusw.ParavirtualizedGraphicsGPUTask` = per-running-VM host-side Metal renderer XPC service (ParavirtualizedGraphics.framework). tart attaches the VZ graphics device unconditionally (`--no-graphics` only skips the host window), so every tart guest gets one live task.

**Measured 2026-07-14 on metal (5-min series, 30 s ticks, 27-32 min post-boot):**
- 1024x768 awake: mean 16.7% of a core (9.4-24.2), RSS ~25 MB
- 800x600 awake: mean 21.1% (11.6-26.3) — the resolution shrink measured NO reduction; CPU is driven by guest frame-submission rate (WindowServer compositing), not encode size
- display asleep (`pmset -a displaysleep 1`, engaged in 1 min, `pmset -g log` confirms "Display is turned off"): **0.0% flat** — frame submission stops entirely. Total win; codified in darwin/metal.nix's pmset line (system sleep stays hard-off: `sleep 0 disksleep 0 powernap 0`).
- The ~2% Activity-Monitor figure from earlier was a multi-day decayed average; fresh boots run 15-25% awake.

**Where displaysleep applies:** metal only. bluebubbles' display does real work (vncdotool iMessage automation — never sleep it); hermes is a serial-console NixOS guest with no compositor (nothing to save).

**Identify the live task:** spawn-time correlation with the `tart run <vm>` process start (cluster spawns within ~20 s of it) + RSS signature (live compositor ~25-32 MB; idle/orphan siblings ~7-12 MB). A guest reboot tears down and respawns the whole cluster (same tart PID); VM stop cleaned up its clusters both times observed — the famous orphan leak (~3 MB each, VirtualBuddy #616) is real but not universal; host reboot reaps orphans.

Related: [[host-serving-migration-2026-07]].
